Fitness assessment,Health standards	High blood pressure
Unconditional licence
The cut-off blood pressure values used to determine fitness for an unconditional licence do not align with standard hypertension management goals.

Incapacity,Risk factors	High blood pressure
Neurological events
Blood pressure levels relevant to licensing are set based on their association with sudden incapacity caused by neurological events like stroke.

Issuance,Requirements	Commercial vehicle driver
Conditional licence
Conditional licences for commercial vehicle drivers are issued by the driver licensing authority based on medical advice.

Advice,Assessment	Commercial vehicle driver
Medical specialist
A medical specialist provides advice to the driver licensing authority regarding the fitness of commercial vehicle drivers.

Agreement,Ongoing assessment	Commercial vehicle driver
General practitioner
The ongoing fitness of a commercial vehicle driver with high blood pressure may be assessed by a general practitioner if mutually agreed upon with the specialist.

Initial recommendation,Opinion	Conditional licence
Medical specialist
The initial recommendation for issuing a conditional licence must be based on the opinion of the medical specialist.

blood pressure,eligibility,medical fitness	Commercial Standards
Unconditional Licence
The commercial standards define that a person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if they have consistently high blood pressure.

criteria,granting,issuance,regulation,review	Conditional Licence
Driver Licensing Authority
The driver licensing authority may consider granting a conditional licence subject to annual review and specific medical criteria.<SEP>The authority considers issuing a conditional licence subject to annual review based on medical criteria.

information provision,initial grant	Conditional Licence
Treating Specialist
The treating specialist provides information regarding the driver's fitness, which must be the basis for the initial granting of a conditional licence.

assessment,collaboration	General Practitioner
Treating Specialist
The treating specialist and general practitioner may collaborate to assess ongoing fitness to drive for commercial vehicle drivers if mutually agreed.

assessment,collaboration,criteria,information	Driver Licensing Authority
Treating Specialist
The treating specialist and driver licensing authority may collaborate to assess ongoing fitness to drive for commercial vehicle drivers if mutually agreed.<SEP>The specialist provides information regarding hypertension control and side effects to the authority for licence consideration.

assessment,collaboration	Driver Licensing Authority
General Practitioner
The general practitioner and driver licensing authority may collaborate to assess ongoing fitness to drive for commercial vehicle drivers if mutually agreed.

health criterion,medical control,medical requirement,requirement	Antihypertensive Therapy
Conditional Licence
A person must be treated with antihypertensive therapy and achieve effective control of hypertension over a 4-week follow-up period to meet criteria for a conditional licence.<SEP>Effective control of hypertension achieved over a four-week period is a required criterion for the licence.

monitoring,side effects	Blood Pressure
Conditional Licence
For a conditional licence, there must be no side effects from medication that will impair safe driving and no evidence of damage to target organs relevant to driving.

blood pressure,eligibility,health criteria	Person
Unconditional Licence
A person is determined to be unfit for holding an unconditional licence if they exhibit consistently high blood pressure levels.

agreement,assessment,fitness	Commercial Vehicle Driver
Treating GP
The GP may assess ongoing fitness to drive for commercial vehicle drivers provided there is mutual agreement among the specialist, GP, and authority.

information provision,initial assessment	Commercial Vehicle Driver
Treating Specialist
The initial granting of a conditional licence for commercial vehicle drivers must be based on information provided by the specialist.
